t: Here stood the Globe Theatre, a Victorian playhouse built in 1868 and demolished in 1902. It was the third London theatre to bear the name, after Shakespeare's Bankside house, which closed in 1642. Its repertoire was mainly comedies and musical shows. It was owned by Sefton Henry Parry, a theatre manager who was also an actor, comedian and playwright. He could paint scenery and do stage carpentry, and he built theatres as well as running them.
